title: Distance-learning platform EAD-online in Belgium reportedly down since a cyberattack, La DH reports
date_note: La DH's article of 24 November says the attack hit in mid-September and the site has been inaccessible for about two months; the page gives no earlier day for the report, so its publication day is used.
geo_basis: Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles named by the source; no city given, pin at Brussels
summary: La DH reports that the e-learning platform of Enseignement à Distance (EAD-online.be) has been inaccessible since a cyberattack in mid-September, with 10.000 pupils deprived of lessons for two months according to its headline. BX1 reported on 5 October that the platform announced the cyberattack and would stay closed until mid-October. La DH says no reopening date is set.
plain: A Belgian distance-learning platform has reportedly been down for about two months after a cyberattack, according to La DH. No reopening date has been given.
exec: A public online school platform has been unavailable for weeks after an attack, per La DH, showing how long recovery of education services can take.

evidence.quote: 10.000 élèves privés de cours depuis deux mois

validation.note: Corroborated by two independent publishers, La DH (dhnet.be) and BX1 (bx1.be), which each state the cyberattack on EAD-online; no official statement page was read.

review.note: Compared mid-September attack, two months offline, 10.000 pupils headline, no reopening date, no attribution against La DH
